Topic5.jsx|E-typed-critical-value|Meaning of the blue line crossing the red line (): The red dashed horizontal line marks the 5% critical threshold (). The point where the blue line intersects the red line marks the Median Detection Threshold . To the left (), the typical sample cannot distinguish the faint signal from noise (, failing to reject). To the right (), the typical sample produces , making the predictive signal reliably detectable in the majority of datasets.|#1

Topic5.jsx|D-typed-percent-in-text|Meaning of the Red curve vs. Green curve (and their gap): The red curve shows the Granger 5% Detection Rate (). At (pure noise), the red curve starts at exactly 5% (the Type I error rate enforced by the test), while the green curve starts at ~50% (both models have identical true capability, so finite-sample holdout errors are a 50/50 coin flip). As increases into mild signals (), the green curve quickly climbs to 60%–75% (unrestricted wins most holdouts), yet the conservative Granger test only detects it in 15%–40% of datasets. When is strong, the red curve surges toward 100% and catches up to the green curve.|#1
